name: Phirni
steps: Rinse rice, soak in plenty of water for 30 minutes, then drain thoroughly. Grind with 60 ml of the measured milk into a coarse paste with tiny grains; avoid a completely smooth paste.
Warm the remaining milk in a heavy saucepan. Take out 20 ml warm milk into a cup and soak the saffron in it. Bring the milk in the pan to a gentle simmer.

Reduce the heat and pour in the rice paste in a thin stream while whisking. Cook for 15–20 minutes, stirring the bottom and corners frequently, until the rice grains are soft and the mixture coats a spoon.
Stir in sugar, cardamom and all the saffron milk. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Keep the phirni slightly loose because it thickens further when chilled.
Divide among 4 shallow bowls. Let the heavy steam subside, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until softly set. Sprinkle pistachios over the chilled phirni before serving.
tips: The rice must be fully cooked before adding sugar. A coarse rice paste gives phirni its delicate grainy texture.
passiveTime: Allow 30 minutes to soak rice and at least 2 hours to chill the finished dessert.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
